An interactive exploration of RLMs — a paradigm enabling LLMs to process arbitrarily long prompts through recursive decomposition and REPL environments.

rlm_demo.pyPseudocode

# RLMs enable 100x context scaling

from rlm import RLM

 

rlm = RLM(backend="openai", backend_kwargs={"model_name": "gpt-5-nano"})

 

# Process 10M tokens with the same interface as a single LLM call

response = rlm.completion(

query="Summarize findings",

context=ten_million_token_doc

)

 

→ ~114% better than GPT-5 on OOLONG

→ Median cheaper per query (outliers may be more expensive)

Key Insights

From the paper authors

“Much like the switch in 2025 from language models to reasoning models, we think 2026 will be all about the switch to Recursive Language Models (RLMs). It turns out that models can be far more powerful if you allow them to treat their own prompts as an object in an external environment.”

Alex Zhang

@a1zhang

2026 will be the year of RLMs
“On the OOLONG benchmark, RLMs with GPT-5-mini outperforms GPT-5 by ~114% gains (more than double!) on 132k-token sequences—nearly as cheap as GPT-5—and is cheaper on average at 263k tokens.”

Alex Zhang

@a1zhang

~114% performance gains with smaller model
“Most people (mis)understand RLMs to be about LLMs invoking themselves. The deeper insight is LLMs interacting with their own prompts as objects.”

Omar Khattab

@lateinteraction

Prompts as manipulable objects
“My favorite part of Alex's post is studying what the recursive LM actually decides to do—how does it take a variable with 10M tokens and figure it out? You see strategies like: peeking, map/reduce, summarization, and output accumulation.”

Omar Khattab

@lateinteraction

Emergent strategies: peeking, map/reduce, summarization

Core Concepts

Four pillars of the RLM paradigm

Recursive Decomposition

Instead of processing a huge prompt all at once, the model breaks it into smaller chunks and processes them recursively, like dividing a big task into sub-tasks.

Explore

REPL Environment

The model operates inside a Python notebook environment where the huge context is stored as a variable. The model writes code to inspect, slice, and process this variable.

Explore

Context Chunking

The model intelligently decides how to split large contexts into manageable pieces, adapting its strategy based on the query and context structure.

Explore

Sub-Query Delegation

The root LM can call smaller LMs (like GPT-5-mini) to answer specific sub-questions about parts of the context, then combine their answers.

Explore
